```{r}
#| label: element-context
#| include: false
# Everything below is driven by SYM, set by the calling page. No page holds a
# number of its own: they all read the same summary CSVs.
e_rows <- elements[elements$symbol == SYM, ]
e_rows <- e_rows[order(match(e_rows$cat, cat_order)), ]
e_name <- e_rows$name[1]
e_cap  <- capability(SYM)
e_bulk <- e_rows[e_rows$cat == "bulk", ]
has_bulk <- nrow(e_bulk) > 0

e_bg  <- backgrounds[backgrounds$symbol == SYM, ]
e_vd  <- verdicts[verdicts$symbol == SYM, ]
e_pr  <- pressure[pressure$symbol == SYM, ]
e_ct  <- controls[controls$symbol == SYM & controls$reliable, ]
# A withheld element gets no distance-band chart. Its surviving concentrations are
# an upper tail, so a median by band would be a number we already know is biased,
# drawn as if it were a reading.
show_pressure <- !any(e_rows$withheld) &&
  nrow(e_pr[e_pr$measure == "concentration" & e_pr$reliable, ]) > 0
show_controls <- !any(e_rows$withheld) && nrow(e_ct) > 0
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr any(e_rows$withheld)
cat("## Why this element is withheld\n\n",
    "The laboratories that measured ", tolower(e_name), " often could not quantify it: ",
    "the value was somewhere below a detection limit rather than a number. Those rows ",
    "are removed during cleaning, which is right for contamination screening and wrong ",
    "for estimating a background.\n\n",
    "A background **is** the low end of a distribution. Delete the low end, and what ",
    "is left is an upper tail that would look like a respectable background and be too ",
    "high. So no background and no verdict is published for ", tolower(e_name),
    ", at any fraction.\n\n", sep = "")
```

```{r}
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 20, linetype = 2, colour = "#b3261e") +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#bbbbbb", `TRUE` = "#CC6677"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +
  labs(x = "Below the limit of quantification (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Where the samples are

```{r}
#| include: false
grid_path <- file.path(sdir, "summary_map_grid.csv")
g <- read.csv(grid_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
g <- g[g$symbol == SYM & g$cat %in% cat_order,
       c("cat", "lat", "lon", "n", "value_p50", "igeo_p50", "n_sites",
         "n_sites_class", "n_sites_strict", "n_sites_ef", "verdict_basis",
         "pristine_class")]
g <- g[order(match(g$cat, cat_order)), ]
if (!nrow(g)) g <- g[0, ]
ojs_define(mapdata = g)
map_has_points <- nrow(g) > 0
# All three fractions, drawn one at a time. Every other table on this page reports
# the three side by side; the map was the one place the sieved samples vanished.
# What must not happen is a shared colour scale across them, so each fraction is
# scaled on its own cells and the page says the colours are not comparable.
map_fracs <- data.frame(cat = intersect(cat_order, unique(g$cat)),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
map_fracs$label <- unname(cat_label[map_fracs$cat])
ojs_define(map_fracs = map_fracs)
# Igeo needs a background, and a withheld element has none, so the grid carries no
# Igeo for it. Offering a colour scale that would paint every cell grey is worse
# than not offering it. The withholding is per element, not per fraction, so this
# one flag covers whichever fraction is being shown.
map_has_igeo <- map_has_points && any(!is.na(g$igeo_p50))
# The pristine layer exists per fraction, not per element: manganese has a verdict
# in the sieved fractions and none in bulk, so the option has to follow whichever
# fraction is on show. A group with no verdict carries no class at all, which is
# not the same as a cell whose sites could not be classified.
# the module writes NA as an empty field, and read.csv hands that back as "" rather
# than NA, so an emptiness test alone would offer a pristine layer for a fraction
# that has no verdict and then draw an empty map under it.
map_pristine_cats <- unique(g$cat[!is.na(g$pristine_class) & nzchar(g$pristine_class)])
ojs_define(map_pristine_cats = data.frame(cat = map_pristine_cats,
                                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
# A withheld element publishes no concentration anywhere else on this page. A cell
# median of what cleared the detection limit is the upper tail the section above
# warns about, so the map keeps the cells and drops the colour scale: it says where
# the element was measured and nothing about how much of it was there.
map_withheld <- any(e_rows$withheld)
ojs_define(map_unit = UNIT)
ojs_define(map_has_igeo = map_has_igeo)
ojs_define(map_withheld = map_withheld)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Which fraction to draw. Only the fractions this element actually has are
// offered, so iodine gets bulk and sieved <63 um and no empty third button.
viewof frac = fracs.length
  ? Inputs.radio(new Map(fracs.map(o => [o.label, o.cat])),
                 { value: fracs[0].cat, label: "Fraction" })
  : Object.assign(html`<span></span>`, { value: "bulk" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
pristine_cats = transpose(map_pristine_cats).map(o => o.cat)

// The options follow the fraction on show, because the verdict does: manganese is
// judged in the sieved fractions and not in bulk. Switching fraction rebuilds this
// radio, which resets it to concentration; that is the honest behaviour when the
// choices themselves have changed.
colour_opts = {
  const o = [["Concentration", "value_p50"]];
  if (map_has_igeo) o.push(["Enrichment (Igeo)", "igeo_p50"]);
  if (pristine_cats.includes(frac)) o.push(["Pristine", "pristine_class"]);
  return o;
}

// The placeholder has to carry a value. Generators.input never yields for an
// element that has none, so `chosen` would stay pending for ever, and every cell
// downstream of it, the map included, would silently never run.
viewof chosen = colour_opts.length > 1
  ? Inputs.radio(new Map(colour_opts), { value: "value_p50", label: "Colour by" })
  : Object.assign(html`<span></span>`, { value: "value_p50" })
layer = chosen
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mapDiv = {
  const div = html`<div id="map"></div>`;
  yield div;
  const map = L.map(div, { zoomControl: true });
  // CARTO's basemaps now watermark every tile with "API key required", so the
  // tiles come straight from OpenStreetMap, as they do on the detailed site.
  L.tileLayer("https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", {
    attribution: "&copy; OpenStreetMap contributors",
    maxZoom: 12
  }).addTo(map);

  // The home view is this element's own extent, not a fixed window on Norway.
  // Copper runs from 36 to 81 north; iodine sits in the Kattegat. The zoom cap
  // stops a sparse element from opening at street level with no coastline for
  // context, and the fallback is the extent of the database as a whole.
  const lats = pts.map(d => d.lat), lons = pts.map(d => d.lon);
  const home = pts.length
    ? L.latLngBounds([Math.min(...lats), Math.min(...lons)],
                     [Math.max(...lats), Math.max(...lons)])
    : L.latLngBounds([36, -25], [81, 40]);
  // Fit to the data, then hold the zoom inside 3 to 6. The cap stops a sparse
  // element opening at street level with no coastline for context. The floor is
  // there because Mercator stretches the far north: fitting copper's 36 to 81
  // degrees honestly would open on a world map with Europe as a smudge in the
  // middle. Three is the zoom the detailed site's maps use.
  const goHome = () => {
    map.invalidateSize();
    map.fitBounds(home, { padding: [24, 24], maxZoom: 6 });
    if (map.getZoom() < 3) map.setView(home.getCenter(), 3);
  };
  goHome();

  const HomeControl = L.Control.extend({
    options: { position: "topleft" },
    onAdd() {
      const btn = L.DomUtil.create("a", "leaflet-home-button");
      btn.href = "#";
      btn.title = "Reset the view";
      btn.setAttribute("aria-label", "Reset the view");
      btn.innerHTML = '<i class="bi bi-house-door" aria-hidden="true"></i>';
      L.DomEvent.on(btn, "click", e => { L.DomEvent.stop(e); goHome(); });
      return btn;
    }
  });
  new HomeControl().addTo(map);

  // One colour for a withheld element, a scale for everything else. Cells still
  // mark where the element was measured; what is dropped is the number.
  const PLAIN = "#3f7fb5";
  // The pristine layer is a verdict, not a level, so it is drawn as classes. The
  // order is best to worst and grey is last on purpose: on the bulk maps grey is
  // the commonest cell by far, and it means the sediment could not be judged, not
  // that it was judged clean.
  const PR_ORDER = ["strict", "ef", "not", "unclassified"];
  const PR = {
    strict:       { colour: "#1a7a3c",
                    ef: "Pristine (strict)", conservative: "Pristine (conservative)" },
    ef:           { colour: "#7cc47f",
                    ef: "Pristine (EF < 1)", conservative: null },
    not:          { colour: "#e08214",
                    ef: "Not pristine", conservative: "Not pristine" },
    unclassified: { colour: "#b4b4b4",
                    ef: "Cannot be classified", conservative: "Cannot be classified" }
  };
  const isPristine = layer === "pristine_class";
  const basis = pts.length ? pts[0].verdict_basis : null;

  let ramp = null, isIgeo = false, barLo = null, barHi = null;
  if (!map_withheld && !isPristine) {
    const vals = pts.map(d => d[layer]).filter(v => v !== null && !isNaN(v));
    if (!vals.length) return;
    const sorted = vals.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b);
    const q = p => sorted[Math.floor(p * (sorted.length - 1))];
    const lo = q(0.05), hi = q(0.95);
    isIgeo = layer === "igeo_p50";
    // Diverging around zero for Igeo, sequential for concentration. Igeo is a log2
    // index whose zero point is "at background", so a scale that does not mark zero
    // would hide the only threshold that means anything.
    ramp = isIgeo
      ? d3.scaleDiverging(d3.interpolateRdBu).domain([Math.max(2, hi), 0, Math.min(-2, lo)])
      : d3.scaleSequential(d3.interpolateViridis).domain([lo, hi]);
    barLo = isIgeo ? Math.min(-2, lo) : lo;
    barHi = isIgeo ? Math.max(2, hi) : hi;
  }

  // The legend. Colour is the only thing on this map carrying a value, so it has
  // to be readable without the popups. The bar is sampled from the same ramp the
  // markers use rather than restating the palette, so a change to the scale
  // cannot leave the legend describing the previous one.
  const fmt = v => Math.abs(v) >= 100 ? v.toFixed(0)
                 : Math.abs(v) >= 10  ? v.toFixed(1)
                 : v.toFixed(2);
  const legendBody = () => {
    if (isPristine) {
      // only the classes this fraction actually has. A sieved fraction has no
      // enrichment factor, so its cells can never carry the EF class and its
      // legend can never name one.
      const present = PR_ORDER.filter(k =>
        PR[k][basis] && pts.some(d => d.pristine_class === k));
      return `<div class="legend-title">Pristine verdict</div>` +
             `<div class="legend-sub">${frac_label}, by cell</div>` +
             present.map(k =>
               `<div class="legend-row">` +
                 `<span class="legend-swatch" style="background:${PR[k].colour}"></span>` +
                 `<span>${PR[k][basis] ?? PR[k].ef}</span>` +
               `</div>`).join("") +
             `<div class="legend-note">A cell takes the strictest class a majority ` +
             `of its sites meet. Grey is a gap in the data, not a clean result.</div>`;
    }
    if (map_withheld) {
      return `<div class="legend-title">Where it was measured</div>` +
             `<div class="legend-sub">${frac_label}</div>` +
             `<div class="legend-row">` +
               `<span class="legend-swatch" style="background:${PLAIN}"></span>` +
               `<span>Cells with data</span>` +
             `</div>` +
             `<div class="legend-note">Concentrations are not mapped for this ` +
             `element. See "Why this element is withheld" above.</div>`;
    }
    const stops = d3.range(0, 1.0001, 1 / 32)
                    .map(t => ramp(barLo + t * (barHi - barLo)));
    // Igeo zero is the only threshold on either scale that means anything, so it
    // gets a tick at its true position, which is not the middle of the bar.
    const zeroPct = 100 * (0 - barLo) / (barHi - barLo);
    return `<div class="legend-title">${isIgeo ? "Enrichment (Igeo)" : "Median concentration"}</div>` +
      `<div class="legend-sub">${frac_label}, ` +
        `${isIgeo ? "0 = at the natural background" : map_unit}</div>` +
      `<div class="legend-barwrap${isIgeo ? " has-zero" : ""}">` +
        `<div class="legend-bar" style="background:linear-gradient(to right,${stops.join(",")})"></div>` +
        (isIgeo ? `<div class="legend-zero" style="left:${zeroPct}%"><span>0</span></div>` : "") +
      `</div>` +
      `<div class="legend-labels"><span>${fmt(barLo)}</span><span>${fmt(barHi)}</span></div>` +
      `<div class="legend-note">` +
        (isIgeo ? "Blue is at or below background, red is above it. " : "") +
        `Cells past either end take the end colour.</div>`;
  };

  const LegendControl = L.Control.extend({
    options: { position: "bottomright" },
    onAdd() {
      const d = L.DomUtil.create("div", "legend");
      d.innerHTML = legendBody();
      L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(d);
      return d;
    }
  });
  new LegendControl().addTo(map);

  const canvas = L.canvas({ padding: 0.5 });
  for (const d of pts) {
    const v = d[layer];
    if (isPristine ? !PR[d.pristine_class]
                   : (!map_withheld && (v === null || isNaN(v)))) continue;
    const fill = isPristine   ? PR[d.pristine_class].colour
               : map_withheld ? PLAIN
                              : ramp(v);
    // the composition, not just the class the majority produced: a cell reported
    // pristine over sites that mostly could not be judged is a different object
    // from one where every site was judged and passed.
    const nUnclass = d.n_sites - d.n_sites_class;
    const popup = isPristine
      ? `sites: ${d.n_sites}<br>` +
        `pristine (strict): ${d.n_sites_strict}<br>` +
        (basis === "ef"
          ? `pristine (EF < 1) only: ${d.n_sites_ef - d.n_sites_strict}<br>` : "") +
        `not pristine: ${d.n_sites_class - d.n_sites_ef}<br>` +
        `no verdict possible: ${nUnclass}`
      : (map_withheld ? "" :
          `median: ${d.value_p50} ${map_unit}<br>` +
          `Igeo: ${d.igeo_p50 ?? "n/a"}<br>`) +
        `measurements: ${d.n}`;
    L.circleMarker([d.lat, d.lon], {
      renderer: canvas, radius: 4, weight: 0.4, color: "#333",
      fillColor: fill, fillOpacity: 0.85
    }).bindPopup(
      `<b>${d.lat.toFixed(1)}, ${d.lon.toFixed(1)}</b><br>` + popup
    ).addTo(map);
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| output: asis

cat("Each point is a 0.1 degree cell (roughly 11 km)")
if (map_withheld) {
  cat(", drawn in a single colour on purpose. A cell median would be the middle of ",
      "the measurements that cleared the detection limit, which is the upper tail ",
      "described above, so the map says where ", tolower(e_name), " was measured and ",
      "nothing about how much of it was there.", sep = "")
} else {
  cat(", coloured by the median of the sites inside it, on the scale shown in the ",
      "legend. That scale runs between the 5th and the 95th percentile of the cells, ",
      "so a few extreme cells share the end colour rather than flattening the range ",
      "everything else sits in. Cells are summaries: a cell containing both clean and ",
      "enriched sites shows the middle of them.", sep = "")
}
cat(" The map opens on the region where the fraction on show was measured, which ",
    "differs from fraction to fraction; the house button returns to that view.\n\n",
    sep = "")

if (length(map_pristine_cats)) {
  cat("Colouring by **Pristine** shows the verdict rather than the level: a cell ",
      "takes the strictest class that a majority of its sites meet, and the popup ",
      "gives the composition behind it. ", sep = "")
  if ("bulk" %in% map_pristine_cats) {
    cat("In bulk sediment most cells cannot be judged at all, because the verdict ",
        "needs aluminium measured beside the metal and aluminium is rarely there ",
        "near the coast or near a fish farm. **A grey cell means the sediment could ",
        "not be judged, not that it was judged clean.** ", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\n\n")
}

if (nrow(map_fracs) > 1) {
  cat("The fractions are drawn one at a time")
  if (map_withheld) {
    cat(". Switching between them changes which samples are on the map, and ",
        "nothing else.\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat(", each scaled on its own cells. They are different materials, so the ",
        "colours do not carry across: a cell that reads dark in bulk and pale in a ",
        "sieved fraction is telling you about the two scales, not about the ",
        "sediment. Compare a fraction with itself across the map, never one ",
        "fraction's colour with another's.\n\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```
